content:
Hot weather can be risky for older and frail people, particularly those living alone or with several health conditions.

This guide covers staying safe in a heatwave. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Staying cool

  • Keep curtains closed on sunny windows.
  • Stay out of the sun between 11am and 3pm.
  • Use a fan, cool showers or damp cloths.
  • Wear loose, light clothing.

Drinking enough

  • Drink regularly, even if not thirsty.
  • Keep drinks within easy reach, in a cup that is easy to hold.
  • If you have been told to limit fluids, ask your GP for advice.

Medicines and heat

Some medicines, such as diuretics or some blood pressure medicines, can affect how you cope with heat. Do not stop medicines, but ask your pharmacist for advice. Store medicines as directed.

Signs of heat exhaustion

Headache, dizziness, nausea, cramps, heavy sweating, and feeling very thirsty. Move somewhere cool, drink and cool down. Get help if not better in 30 minutes.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for heatstroke signs: confusion, fits, loss of consciousness, or feeling hot and dry and not sweating.
  • Call NHS 111 if heat exhaustion symptoms do not improve after 30 minutes of cooling.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Does heat affect arthritis?

Some people notice changes. Heat-related illness is the main concern in frailty.

Who should I check on?

Older neighbours, especially those living alone.

Sources and further reading

  • NHS: Heatwave: how to cope in hot weather
  • Age UK: Understanding frailty
